review:
SUMMARY: 10 confirmed bugs identified across AI, config, lock, common, and client modules, primarily involving unguarded parsing, null-safety violations, misleading error messages, iterator exhaustion, and map pollution.

POINTS:
- [ai/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/ai/utils/SkillZipParser.java:233] Misleading error "SKILL.md file not found in zip" thrown when the file actually exists but is blank/empty [— fix: change message to "SKILL.md file is blank or empty"]
- [config/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/config/server/configuration/ConfigChangeConfigs.java:61] StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when property name lacks a dot, as indexOf('.') returns -1 and is passed directly to substring(0, typeIndex) [— fix: guard substring call with typeIndex != -1 check]
- [lock/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/lock/core/reentrant/AbstractAtomicLock.java:275] NullPointerException in removeStaleWaiter when entry.getOwner() is null, due to unsafe .equals(owner) call [— fix: use Objects.equals(entry.getOwner(), owner)]
- [common/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/common/utils/StringUtils.java:198-216] Trailing separator bug in join() when collection has trailing nulls, as separator logic relies on array index instead of remaining non-null elements [— fix: refactor loop to only append separator when a subsequent non-null element exists]
- [common/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/common/utils/CollectionUtils.java:144-175] size() exhausts Iterator/Enumeration by calling next()/nextElement(), destroying state for any subsequent iteration
- [lock/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/lock/service/impl/LockOperationServiceImpl.java:308] expireLock creates zombie empty lock entries via computeIfAbsent when lock doesn't exist, polluting the map and wasting memory
- [lock/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/lock/core/reentrant/mutex/ReentrantAtomicLock.java:53] NullPointerException in tryLock when lockInfo.getOwner() is null, due to unsafe requestOwner.equals(owner) call [— fix: swap to owner.equals(requestOwner)]
- [client-basic/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/client/auth/ram/identify/StsConfig.java:70] NumberFormatException crash at startup if nacos.ram.refreshTime is non-numeric, due to unprotected Integer.parseInt [— fix: wrap parse in try-catch and fall back to default value on failure]
- [client-basic/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/client/address/EndpointServerListProvider.java:242] NumberFormatException crash if endpoint port property is non-numeric, due to unprotected Integer.parseInt [— fix: use NumberUtils.toInt(endpointPortTmp, this.endpointPort) for safe fallback parsing]
- [ai/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/ai/importer/config/AiResourceImportProperties.java:192] NumberFormatException crash at startup if AI resource import config properties are non-numeric, due to unprotected Integer.parseInt/Long.parseLong [— fix: wrap parsing in try-catch blocks returning defaults on failure]

suspicions.observation: ReentrantAtomicLock.doTryLock() line 53 calls requestOwner.equals(owner) where requestOwner comes from lockInfo.getOwner() which could be null. The parent class AbstractAtomicLock.tryLock() only checks lockInfo != null but doesn't validate lockInfo.getOwner() != null.
suspicions.suspected_bug: NullPointerException when tryLock is called with LockInfo whose owner field is null, because requestOwner.equals(owner) is called without null check on requestOwner

suspicions.observation: In StringUtils.join(Collection, String), when iterating with index i, the separator is appended based on index position (i != collection.size() - 1), not based on whether there are more non-null elements. When the collection contains trailing null elements, a spurious trailing separator is produced. For example, join(["a", null], ",") produces "a," instead of "a".
suspicions.suspected_bug: Trailing separator bug: join(["a", null], ",") returns "a," with trailing comma, because the null-skipping logic doesn't account for the separator being added before a null element. The separator decision is based on array index, not on whether subsequent non-null elements exist.

suspicions.observation: In CollectionUtils.size(Object object) at lines 152-157 and 158-163, when the object is an Iterator or Enumeration, the method exhausts the entire iterator/enumeration by calling next()/nextElement() to count elements. This destroys the iterator state as a side effect, which is unexpected and potentially dangerous since the caller may have intended to use the iterator after calling size().
suspicions.suspected_bug: Calling size() on an Iterator or Enumeration exhausts it, consuming all elements. Any subsequent use of the same iterator will find it empty. This is a contract violation where the caller expects a size query to be non-destructive.

suspicions.observation: In SkillZipParser.parseSkillFromZip at line 230-233, when skillMdContent is blank (empty/whitespace), the error message says "SKILL.md file not found in zip" - but the file WAS found (null check at line 223 already passed). The actual problem is that the file is BLANK, not missing. This is a copy-paste error of the error message from the null check above.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Users get misleading error "SKILL.md file not found in zip" when the actual problem is that SKILL.md is blank/empty, making debugging harder

suspicions.observation: In LockOperationServiceImpl.expireLock() at line 308, lockManager.getMutexLock(lockInfo.getKey()) is called which uses computeIfAbsent (as shown in the test at line 219), creating a new empty lock even when the lock doesn't exist. The expireLock method then operates on this zombie lock. Meanwhile, releaseLock() at line 168 uses lockManager.showLocks().get() which does NOT create the lock. This inconsistency means expireLock can pollute the lock map with empty locks that will never be removed (line 334 removes only when no waiters exist, but the lock was just created empty).
suspicions.suspected_bug: expireLock creates zombie (empty) lock entries in the lock map when the lock doesn't exist, because getMutexLock() uses computeIfAbsent. These zombie entries accumulate over time and waste memory. releaseLock() correctly uses showLocks().get() which doesn't create entries.

suspicions.observation: In StsConfig constructor at line 70, Integer.parseInt(timeToRefreshInMillisecond) is called without try-catch when the property is non-blank. If the user sets the property to a non-numeric value like "abc" or "1000ms", this will throw NumberFormatException and crash client startup. The isBlank check only verifies non-null/non-empty, not that the value is actually numeric.
suspicions.suspected_bug: NumberFormatException crash at client startup if the nacos.ram.refreshTime property is set to a non-numeric string, because Integer.parseInt has no try-catch protection

suspicions.observation: In EndpointServerListProvider.initEndpointPort() at line 242, Integer.parseInt(endpointPortTmp) is called without any numeric validation or try-catch. If the endpoint port property is set to a non-numeric value, this will throw NumberFormatException. While StringUtils.isNotBlank() is checked, it doesn't validate the value is actually an integer.
suspicions.suspected_bug: NumberFormatException crash if endpoint port property is set to a non-numeric string, because Integer.parseInt has no try-catch

suspicions.observation: In AbstractAtomicLock.removeStaleWaiter(String owner) at line 275, entry.getOwner().equals(owner) is called without null check on entry.getOwner(). Compare with the sibling method removeWaiter at line 299 which uses Objects.equals(entry.getOwner(), owner) - null safe. If a WaitEntry with null owner exists in the queue (possible since WaitEntry has no validation on owner), removeStaleWaiter will throw NPE while removeWaiter would handle it gracefully.
suspicions.suspected_bug: NullPointerException in removeStaleWaiter when a WaitEntry with null owner is in the queue, because entry.getOwner().equals(owner) is called without null check on entry.getOwner()

suspicions.observation: In AiResourceImportProperties.getInt() at line 192, Integer.parseInt(value) is called without try-catch when the property value is non-blank. If the property is set to a non-numeric string, this will throw NumberFormatException. Same issue at line 197 for Long.parseLong(). This is in the config loading path which runs at startup.
suspicions.suspected_bug: NumberFormatException crash at startup if AI resource import config properties are set to non-numeric values, because getInt() and getLong() lack try-catch around Integer.parseInt/Long.parseLong

suspicions.observation: In ConfigChangeConfigs.refreshPluginProperties() at line 60-62, int typeIndex = each.indexOf('.') is used and then each.substring(0, typeIndex) is called. If the property name doesn't contain a dot, indexOf('.') returns -1, and substring(0, -1) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The surrounding try-catch will swallow it but the properties won't be loaded correctly.
suspicions.suspected_bug: StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when a config property name under the PREFIX doesn't contain a dot, because indexOf('.') returns -1 and is used directly as substring end index

suspicions.observation: In FuzzyGroupKeyPattern.matchPattern() at line 109, String[] splitPatterns = groupKeyPattern.split(">>") is called. Then at line 110-112, splitPatterns[0], splitPatterns[1], and splitPatterns[2] are accessed directly. If the groupKeyPattern doesn't contain the ">>" delimiter (or contains fewer than 2 occurrences), split() will return an array with fewer than 3 elements, and accessing splitPatterns[1] or splitPatterns[2] will throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
suspicions.suspected_bug: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in matchPattern() when groupKeyPattern is malformed (contains fewer than 2 ">>" delimiters), since splitPatterns[1] and splitPatterns[2] are accessed without bounds checking

solutions.fix_diff:
No fix applied. The bug is that CollectionUtils.size() exhausts Iterator/Enumeration by consuming elements via next()/nextElement() in a while loop.

The correct fix per spec would be to throw IllegalArgumentException for Iterator/Enumeration types, since:
1. A "size()" query method should have no side effects (per Java Collection.size() contract)
2. There is no way to determine the size of an Iterator/Enumeration without consuming elements
3. Neither Iterator nor Enumeration provides a size() method or non-destructive count mechanism

However, applying this fix causes 3 test failures (including the existing testSize() which tests Iterator/Enumeration assertions), compared to the original 2 failures. The new regression tests (testSizeShouldNotExhaustIterator, testSizeShouldNotExhaustEnumeration) expect size() to return normally without exhausting the iterator, which is fundamentally impossible for these Java interface types.

The test's expectation contradicts the spec: you cannot query the size of a forward-only Iterator/Enumeration non-destructively. Recording fixed=false as instructed.
solutions.fix_rerun:
Original state (buggy code): 2 failures (testSizeShouldNotExhaustIterator, testSizeShouldNotExhaustEnumeration)
Throw fix: 3 errors (adds testSize failure from Iterator/Enumeration assertions)
Both scenarios leave tests failing. The test expectations (non-destructive size query on Iterator/Enumeration) contradict Java interface capabilities.

The fix changes expireLock to use showLocks().get() instead of getMutexLock(), preventing zombie lock entry creation for non-existent locks. This aligns with how releaseLock and cancelWaitInternal work.

Results:
- testExpireLockShouldNotCreateEntryForNonExistentLock: Core assertion PASSES (no zombie created). Only fails due to UnnecessaryStubbingException because getMutexLock is correctly NOT called.
- testExpireLockCreatesZombieEntryWhenLockAlreadyRemoved: FAILS - this test ASSERTS buggy behavior (that zombie exists). Fix is correct, test is wrong.
- testExpireLock / testExpireLockNotifiesWaiterAndIgnoresNotificationFailure: FAIL - incompatible mock setup (stub getMutexLock but not showLocks), designed around buggy code path.

The production fix is correct per the spec and sibling code pattern. The test failures are due to test design issues (strict stubbing, asserting buggy behavior, incomplete mock setup) not production code issues.
